the mode coupling has a profound effect on the conductance of the ballistic dot and its magnetoconductance.

the formation of a quantum wire has a significant influence on both the average conductance and the excitation of orbits within the cavity.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the conductance fluctuations of ballistic quantum dots are strongly dependent on the number and coupling of input and output modes.
, in the ballistic limit, the number of modes propagating in the input and output leads is not the only factor determining the magnitude of conductance fluctuations.
mode coupling can be used to control the excitation of different orbits and thus the magnitude of the conductance fluctuations.
